problem: Users and critics objected to the removed Start button and the Start screen.
title: Microsoft restores the Start button and boot-to-desktop in Windows 8.1
context: Windows 8 removed the Start button, which had been part of the desktop since Windows 95, and defaulted to a full-screen Start screen.
decision_made: Bring back a Start button and add an option to boot straight to the desktop in Windows 8.1.
action_taken: Announced on the Windows Blog in May 2013, with a preview in June and a free update later that year.
observed_outcome: The Start button returned, though it did not restore the old menu. The change was described by media as a response to backlash.
lessons: Removing a familiar interface element can force a partial rollback even when the new design is intentional.
limitations: Partial reversal only. Sales and satisfaction effects were not measured in the sources used.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft announced Windows 8.1 would bring back a Start button and offer boot-to-desktop.
The returning button did not bring back the full old Start menu.
